text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
* French drinks company Remy Martin is negotiating to buy port wine company Porto Calem. The terms of the deal have yet to be agreed. Porto Calem is believed to be worth around 3.2 billion escudos.
* Portugal deplored the expulsion of its ambassador from South Africa over the leaking of a misdirected note from President Nelson Mandela to Indonesian President Suharto.
* Oil company Petrogal posted a profit of 1.9 billion escudos in the first six months of 1997, down from 4.5 billion in the same year-ago period.

* Only six percent of the one million shares put up for sale in steel company SN-Produtos Longos were sold at a special session of Lisbon bourse yesterday. Shares that were not sold will be purchased by Atlansider, the consortium that won control of an 80 percent stake in the company.

* The number of investment funds in Portugal is increasing. By the end of the first semester of 1997, the Portuguese Association of Investment Fund Managers registered 30 more funds than in the same period last year.
* Financial services group BPI will dismiss about 1,300 employees in the next two years, by offering early retirement or rescinding contracts.
* British Petroleum said it had formed a 50:50 joint venture with Portuguese grocery retailer Modelo Continente SGPS, owned by Sonae, to build stores alongside BP filling stations in Portugal.
* The government may launch a state company to manage forests before the end of 1997.
